newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-STADLER AND WADKINS TAKE ONE-SHOT LEAD AT SHARK SHOOTOUT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-STADLER AND WADKINS TAKE ONE-SHOT LEAD AT SHARK SHOOTOUT.

text.p: The team of
Craig Stadler and Lanny Wadkins blistered the course in the
best-ball competition to take a one-stroke lead after two
rounds at the $1.1 million Shark Shootout Saturday.
Stadler and Wadkins combined for a best-ball record
15-under-par 57, including an eagle on the 10th hole, to move
to 18-under 126 for the tournament. Wadkins teamed with Tom
Purtzer to win this event in 1990.
Jay Haas and Tom Kite, who were tied for third entering
Saturday's round, eagled the 13th hole en route to a 60 for a
two-round total of 127.
Stadler and Wadkins recorded seven birdies on the front
nine, including two from 25 feet out on the fourth and sixth
holes and an 18-footer on the third hole.
The duo continued their torrid pace on the final nine
holes, starting with Wadkins' eagle on 10 from 105 yards out,
using a pitching wedge. After a couple of tap-in birdies on 11
and 13, Stadler sank a birdie putt from 30 yards out on 14.
Wadkins and Stadler completed their record round with birdies
on the final three holes.
"It was a lot of fun," said Wadkins. "We both were in play
all of the time. We holed some shots but at the same time we
felt like we could make it. He (Stadler) got ticked off at me
when I missed it (birdie putt) on five."
"I've been playing well and putting better," said Stadler.
"I got it close on most of the holes. We got it on a roll to
a point where we expected a birdie on every hole. We are
20-under the last 27 holes. That's not bad."
Haas and Kite started their round strong with birdies on
the first three holes. Kite completed the front nine by
sinking a 30-foot birdie putt with a pitching wedge on nine.
Haas and Kite stepped up their play on the back nine,
recording birdies on four of the next five holes, sandwiched
around Kite's 30-foot eagle putt on the par-5, 457-yard 13th
hole. Kite added birdies from 40 and 10 feet out on the 16th
and 18th holes, respectively, to finish the round.
"I played very well, but we teamed together so well," said
Kite. "When I was in trouble, he (Haas) was there. I like the
way Jay and I are playing when we are driving it well. We got
past the toughest format today. We know we'll have to take it
low."
"My partner (Kite) shot a 63 today," said Haas. "He was by
himself most of the day. Fortunately I made three birdies on
holes he didn't to at least help. It can't hurt to have two
balls in play all the time. We've done that."
Hale Irwin teamed with Lee Janzen to card a 61 to move to
15-under. Mark O'Meara and Curtis Strange, who held a share of
the first-round lead with Chip Beck and Scott Hoch, combined
for a 64 to finish at 14-under.
The duo of Brad Faxon and Peter Jacobsen combined for a 63
to move to 13-under, followed by Greg Norman, the host of the
tournament, and two-time champion Raymond Floyd at 12-under
and John Daly and David Duval at 11-under.
